2609.18407.title: TERN: A Delta-rule Memory with a Seasonal Reference and Online Adaptation for Epidemic Forecasting
2609.18407.paper_summary: Weekly influenza surveillance counts guide vaccine distribution and public-health alerts, yet they are hard to forecast. Each region offers only a few seasons, waves shift in timing and height every year, and information that helps while a wave grows misleads after its peak, whereas last season's shape stays informative for a year. Existing epidemic graph models and general forecasters read a short fixed window and treat all past information alike, so they neither exploit earlier seasons nor discard stale associations when the epidemic phase changes. To address these limitations, we propose TERN, a forecaster built around a delta-rule fast-weight memory that decays channel-wise and erases along a learned address under gates driven by local epidemic-phase features, combined with an explicit seasonal reference and online adaptation. On three Cola-GNN influenza benchmarks, TERN outperformed epidemic graph models and general forecasters, matched or exceeded seasonal references, and a controlled comparison confirmed the contribution of the memory itself.
2609.18407.paper_summary_zh: 每週流感監測數據指導疫苗分發和公共衛生警報，但它們難以預測。每個地區僅提供幾個季節，波峰的時間和高度每年都在變化，而在波峰增長期間有助於預測的信息在波峰過後則會誤導，然而上季的形狀在一年內仍然具有參考價值。現有的流行病圖模型和一般預測器僅讀取短期固定窗口，並將所有過去的信息視為相同，因此它們既不利用早期季節的信息，也不在流行病階段變化時丟棄過時的關聯。為了解決這些限制，我們提出了TERN，一種基於快速加權記憶的預測器，該記憶根據通道逐漸衰減，並在由當地流行病階段特徵驅動的閘門下沿著學習到的地址進行擦除，結合了明確的季節參考和在線適應。在三個Cola-GNN流感基準上，TERN的表現超過了流行病圖模型和一般預測器，達到了或超過了季節參考，並且控制比較確認了記憶本身的貢獻。
2609.18407.author: Shunya Nagashima et.al.
